trial_court: Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Hadgaon and Family Court at Aurangabad
case_name: Manisha Madhukar Jadhav Nee Manisha ... vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: 01 Manisha w/o Madhukar Jadhav, 02 Madhukar s/o Dattarao Jadhav (Applicants)
parties.respondent_defendant: 01 The State of Maharashtra; 02 The Police Station Officer, Mantha Police Station, Tq. Hadgaon, District Nanded (Respondents)

facts_of_case: Parties arrived at an amicable settlement for setting aside proceedings of Regular Criminal Case No. 88/2019, pending before the Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Hadgaon.

legal_principles.principle: Criminal cases arising from matrimonial discord can be quashed if the parties have settled their dispute.
legal_principles.held: The power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303
Kulwinder Singh v. State of Punjab (2007) 4 CTC 769

legal_principles.principle: Heinous and serious offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be quashed even if the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled their dispute.
legal_principles.held: Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303

outcome.final_order: Proceedings quashed; parties agreed to get separated permanently and withdrawn all adverse allegations made against each other.
